trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 are yours — there is no extra task behind it. Work the roadmap in order: story first, the one missable as you travel, activities and collectibles second, and the 100% completion gold last. Keep this tracker open while you play and the platinum is simply the sum of everything below.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn — just play through the introduction until the mission-complete screen. Use it to learn the basics: driving, the new movement and the wanted system, because every later mission builds on them. Nothing here can be missed.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks at the chapter-complete screen. Chapters in GTA VI run in order, so there is no way to skip ahead — follow the mission markers and the chapter closes itself. If you are chasing the missable meditation trophy, start ticking off spots in this chapter while the map is still small.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Complete all of Chapter 2's missions. By now the map opens up and side activities appear — it is worth sampling one of each activity type as you go, since Master of None only needs a single try at all nine. Keep an eye out for meditation spots while travelling between missions.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 in full. The middle of the story is where most of the mission strands branch, so check your mission list after each story beat — the stranger and contact missions that feed later trophies start appearing here. This is also a good point to bank some cash toward the garage and spending goals.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Complete every mission in Chapter 4. The late story missions are longer and harder, so stock up on armour and ammo before the big set-pieces and use cover — dying restarts a checkpoint, not the chapter, so push through. Once this pops, only the final mission stands between you and the story gold.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. It is the longest mission in the game, so set aside an uninterrupted session and make a manual save before starting — the ending locks in once it is done. After the credits, free roam stays open, so anything you have not finished (collectibles, challenges, the 100% gold) can still be done.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a story mission — follow the marker when it appears in your mission list and play it through to the end. If a mission is not showing, advance the story: contact missions unlock in sequence, so the next story beat is usually what opens it. No special loadout is needed.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist mission. Heists in GTA reward preparation: buy armour, bring a weapon you are accurate with, and follow the plan the game lays out rather than improvising. The trophy unlocks on the mission-complete screen, and the heist payout helps with the money trophies later.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission that appears in the mission list once the story reaches it. Play it through — the objective is straightforward and the mission is short. If it is not available yet, keep playing story missions until the contact offers it.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission — take it from the mission marker and see it through. Missions with a lot of driving are easier in a fast car you have already upgraded, so grab one from your garage before you start. The trophy pops at mission complete.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a story mission centred on the airport. Expect a heavy shootout, so go in with full armour and a rifle with plenty of reserve ammo. Use cover and the Combat Focus slow-down for the tightest stretches — this is also good practice for the Gunslinger trophy.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a late-story mission. It is one of the harder combat missions, so treat it like a set-piece: stock armour, keep a shotgun for close quarters and a rifle for distance, and use your partner as a distraction when the game offers the option. The trophy unlocks when the mission ends.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% in the in-game completion stat — the last gold before the platinum. 100% counts story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the assorted challenges, so it is effectively a summary of every other trophy: there is no separate grind beyond finishing everything else. Check the stats menu to see which category is still short, then work that list. Do the story and the missable first so the cleanup is only counting, not replaying.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, long airtime and the like all count, and the counter runs across the whole game, so normal driving racks it up. To grind it fast, find a jump or ramp you can hit repeatedly in a fast car and loop it; each clean landing with airtime ticks the count. 250 sounds like a lot, but a dedicated session of ramp runs clears it quickly once you have a good spot.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types once — you only need to start and finish (or attempt) one of each, not win or master any of them. The activity types are the ones the game tracks in its activities menu: races, shooting range, fishing, arcade games, drone races and the rest. Open the activities list, work down it one by one, and the trophy pops on the ninth. Do this early, while you are sampling the map anyway.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each challenge has a score threshold for gold — the key is accuracy over speed: take the extra half-second to line up headshots, control recoil in short bursts, and learn each range layout before going for the gold run. Use the weapon the challenge gives you rather than fighting it, and retry a single challenge as many times as you need — progress saves per challenge, so clear them one at a time.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Drone races are about clean lines, not top speed: cut corners where the course allows, avoid the obstacles that spin you out, and learn each course with a slow first lap before racing it properly. The locations are spread across Leonida, so pair this with the exploration trophy and tick locations off as you travel.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different courses count, repeats of the same course do not. Pick a fast, stable car and learn the racing lines: brake before corners, not in them, and use slipstream on the straights. Work through the race list in the activities menu so you can see which courses you have already won; 20 is less than half the list, so you can skip the ones you hate.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are timing-based: watch the line tension, reel in when the fish runs toward you and ease off when it pulls hard, or the line snaps. Cal is a named rival, so the challenge appears through the fishing activity once you have tried it — keep fishing at different spots until his challenge unlocks, then beat his catch. Lighter tackle makes the fight harder but the reward is the same trophy either way.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game — any arcade cabinet, any game, just reach its end screen. Arcade games are short and self-contained, so pick the one you find easiest and learn its pattern; most take only a few minutes. Arcades are marked on the map once you have discovered one, and this also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's last mission. Contact mission strands unlock one mission at a time — after each Andy mission, wait for his next call or check the mission marker on the map. The final mission in a strand is usually the hardest of the set, so go in stocked. The trophy pops when the strand closes.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's last mission. Kenton's strand builds mission by mission; the game tells you when a new one is available, usually by phone call or a marker. Play the strand through in order — you cannot jump to the finale early — and the trophy unlocks at the end of his last mission.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's last mission. Billy's missions are the rougher end of the contact work — expect combat and driving in equal measure. Keep a fast car nearby for the getaways and armour on hand for the shootouts. The strand ends with this mission and the trophy.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish 8 stranger strands — the ? markers scattered across Leonida. Each strand is a short chain of missions for a stranger; the game marks them on the map once you are near, and they stay available in free roam after the story. Work through them region by region while you are exploring for the 52 areas anyway. Eight strands is the silver — there are more strangers than that, so you can skip any strand you dislike.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's last mission. Randy's strand is one of the contact chains — take his missions as they come and the finale unlocks after the earlier ones. The last mission tends to be a set-piece, so save before it and go in prepared. Trophy pops on completion.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's last mission. Tyrone's missions unlock in sequence like the other contacts — the game will point you to the next one. His strand leans on driving and escapes, so keep a quick car in your garage. Complete the finale and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots — and this is the ONE missable trophy, so read this first. Meditation spots are quiet places scattered across Leonida; each one needs you to stop and meditate there, and the game does not hand you a checklist. Tick them off as you travel during the story, especially in the early chapters while the map is small: do a spot whenever you pass one, and use this tracker's list to remember which are done. If you finish the story without all 18, the only way back is an earlier save — so do not leave this for cleanup.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's hunt is a stranger strand: he points you at a specific animal, and you need to track it, get close without spooking it, and take the shot. Use a scoped rifle, approach downwind, and move slowly — animals bolt at noise and fast movement. The trophy unlocks when the hunt is complete and you report back to Bret.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden across Leonida — in shops, on rooftops, in out-of-the-way corners — and a set is complete when you hold every card in it. There are more sets than the three you need, so focus on the sets whose cards cluster in areas you already explore. Check your collection in the menu to see which cards you are missing, then sweep those districts methodically.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK spots are photo points across the state — open the WAiNK app at a marked spot and take the shot. 100 is a long count, so fold it into everything else: snap a spot whenever you pass one during missions, races and exploration, instead of grinding all 100 in one go. The app shows which spots you have already done, so you can mop up the last few by region at the end.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Finish 50 challenges. Challenges are the small goals the game tracks — stunt jumps, kill counts, driving feats, activity scores and more — and they tick over naturally as you play. The counter is cumulative across all types, so 50 arrives on its own during a normal playthrough; if you are close at the end, open the challenges list and pick off the nearly-done ones first.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escape. Build the heat deliberately: cause chaos in a busy area until four stars show, then break line of sight and get moving — the partner needs to stay with you, so use a car and keep them in it. Lose the cops by hiding in alleys, switching vehicles, or putting distance between you and the search area until the stars clear. Do it in a quieter district so the escape route is not swarming.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level — the trick is that you must KEEP the heat, not lose it. Hit three shops in a row in the same area, fast: rob, get back in the car, drive to the next one, and do not let the wanted level drop between robberies. Pick three shops close together, plan the route before the first robbery, and keep your partner with you throughout.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Every new vehicle you get into counts the first time — cars, bikes, boats, trucks and the oddities all add to the total. The counter grows fastest when you try everything you see instead of sticking to one favourite car: hop into a new ride whenever you pass one, even for a few seconds. 100 is most of the way through a normal playthrough if you vary your rides.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies in one Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-down aiming mode — trigger it when a group of enemies is bunched up, and the slowed time lets you line up five clean shots before it runs out. Set it up deliberately: find a mission or gang shootout with five or more enemies close together, wait for them to group, then activate and work left to right with headshots. A rifle with a big magazine helps so you do not reload mid-focus.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the airport. The trick is to leave the airport in a way the schedule never intended: steal a plane from the tarmac and take off, or otherwise get airborne from VCIA without going through the terminal. Any aircraft on the field works; line up on a runway, build speed, and get wheels-up. The trophy pops once you are airborne and clear of the airport.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the military tanks that roll in at high wanted levels. The practical way: get to a wanted level where Rhinos deploy, then deal with one — sticky bombs on the rear, a rocket launcher, or luring it somewhere you can hit it from cover all work. You do not need to destroy a fleet; handle the one that comes for you and the trophy is yours. Keep armour and an escape vehicle ready, because a Rhino's cannon ends fights fast.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth job: go in quiet, move slowly, avoid the cameras' cones and the staff's line of sight, and grab the goods without raising the alarm. If anyone spots you, the attempt fails — leave and try again. Night is easier than day, and a suppressed weapon helps if a guard gets too close. Plan the exit before you go in.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Bank vaults are the big robberies: each one needs a plan, a crew approach and a clean getaway. Do them one at a time across the map rather than back-to-back — the heat after each vault is the hard part, so have a fast car stashed nearby and a route out of the district planned before you go in. Five vaults is the silver; the payout also feeds the money trophies.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks patrol the roads — spot one, block it or force it to stop, then crack it open and take the cash. The truck's guards will fight back and the police will come, so hit it somewhere with a quick escape route and a car waiting. One clean robbery and escape is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. The map tracks which areas you have visited — open it and look for the districts you have never set foot in, then drive or fly through them. This pairs perfectly with everything else: the WAiNK spots, the card hunt, the drone races and the stranger strands all pull you into new corners. Mop up the last few areas deliberately at the end by flying a grid pattern over the state.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation of each of the 9 gangs. Illegal operations are gang-run spots on the map — each gang holds different turf, so you will need to travel the whole state. Hitting one means fighting that gang's crew and getting out with the goods; go in armed and leave fast. Work through the gangs one by one and the trophy pops on the ninth.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to the Ocean Beach waterfront, find a bar with a view over the water, and order a cocktail — the game tracks the moment, not the drink. It is a quiet, missable-in-spirit moment rather than a challenge: go at sunset for the view the trophy describes, sit down, and let the scene play. No combat, no timer, just the beach.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive a car through the showroom's front window and out the other side — the classic GTA exit. Pick a showroom with a clear run-up, build speed, and aim for the glass; the game recognises the smash-and-exit the moment you are back on the street. It is pure spectacle, so enjoy it.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go to the alley, pick up a ball, and bowl — the trophy is about the follow-through, so complete a full game or at least a proper delivery rather than just walking in. Bowling is one of the nine activity types, so this also ticks Master of None if you have not done it yet.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal. This one is about the two leads doing something together that the whole state notices — it unlocks through a story or partner moment rather than a checklist, so keep playing the story with your partner and it will come. If it has not popped by the late story, check the partner activities: the mass-appeal moment is a shared one, not a solo grind.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — the game tracks a count up to 500. This is a cumulative trophy for decisions: dialogue choices, approach choices in missions, and the small either/or moments scattered through the story and free roam. There is no single trick; just play the game making choices instead of idling through them, and the count climbs. It pops once the counter hits its mark.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. Fail something, then succeed at the immediate retry — the trophy is for the comeback, not the failure. The easiest way: attempt a challenge or activity you can retry on the spot (a race, a shooting challenge, a stunt), fail it once, then pass it on the next attempt. The game counts the retry, and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange. Leonida is full of odd, unscripted moments — strange encounters, weird events and easter eggs tucked into the world. This trophy is for stumbling into one: explore off the beaten path, check out the strange markers and the places that look out of place, and let the weirdness find you. There is no checklist for it; it is the game's way of rewarding curiosity.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by. Get in a car, pull up alongside a pedestrian, and hit them with a melee attack from the vehicle — the drive-by melee, not a gun and not running them over. Slow the car to a crawl beside your target so the swing connects, and the trophy pops on the knockdown. Pick a quiet street so the cops do not complicate it.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from heists and robberies — they cannot be spent directly, so launder them through your contacts a batch at a time. The $250,000 is cumulative, so keep laundering every batch you earn instead of letting it pile up. Heists and bank vaults are the fastest source of marked bills, so this pairs with the robbery trophies.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The counter is cumulative across every shop in the game — clothes, weapons, car mods, food, everything. It arrives naturally if you buy gear as you go; if you are short at the end, the fastest way is car modifications, which eat money quickly. Do not hoard cash for this one — spending is the point, and the money trophies want you rich first, generous second.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought through the in-game property market — each one costs money and gives you storage, so they are worth buying as you can afford them. Eight is the full set; check the property listings to see which ones you still lack, and save the most expensive for last when the heist money is flowing. The trophy pops on the eighth purchase.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app lets you register vehicles you own or find — open it with a vehicle and add it to your list. Ten different vehicles is the target, so vary what you register: cars, bikes and the stranger rides all count as long as they are different. Pair it with the 100-vehicle discovery trophy and register as you go.
trophies.name: On the Spot
